stem: In the context of Australian clinical definitions, what is the typical peak age of incidence for bronchiolitis compared to croup?

options.text: Bronchiolitis peaks at 2 years, while croup peaks at 3 to 6 months.
Bronchiolitis peaks at 3 to 6 months, while croup peaks at 2 years.
Both conditions peak at 12 months of age during the winter season.
Bronchiolitis peaks at 6 months to 6 years, while croup is limited to the first year of life.

explanation: Bronchiolitis is predominantly an illness of infancy, whereas croup has a wider age range and peaks in the preschool years.
rationale: Think about which condition is primarily associated with infants under one year of age.

optionExplanations.A: These peaks are reversed; bronchiolitis typically affects younger infants while croup affects older toddlers.
optionExplanations.B: Bronchiolitis is predominantly an illness of infancy, whereas croup has a wider age range and peaks in the preschool years.
optionExplanations.C: While both occur in young children, their specific developmental peaks and seasonal trends differ.
optionExplanations.D: Croup has a much broader age range (up to 6 years) compared to the primary infant focus of bronchiolitis.
